the areas of high attenuation on delayed-phase CT in the liver corresponded histologically with fibrotic areas of various degrees, including those with inflammatory changes.
the delayed enhancement of fibrosis is a characteristic feature of the postequilibrium phase of hepatic tumors and that this feature is useful in differential diagnosis.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the areas of delayed enhancement in hepatic masses corresponded histologically mainly to fibrotic areas and that these areas were not necessarily necrotic or hemorrhagic areas.
the delayed phase CT is useful in differentiating the benign from the malignant hepatic mass and in evaluating the degree of fibrosis in the malignant mass.
delayed enhancement in focal hepatic lesions is due to fibrosis, and the fibrotic areas are related to the degree of malignancy of the lesion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
delayed enhancement on CT may reflect the degree of fibrosis, and the degree of fibrous change may be a prognostic factor for cholangiocellular carcinoma.
CT can provide a clue to the diagnosis of a fibrotic lesion, and the areas of delayed enhancement can be used to differentiate fibrosis from tumor.
the presence of delayed enhancement on contrast-enhanced CT does not necessarily indicate malignancy in hepatic tumors.
